clue.text: Dorothy to get on despite suffering from senility

parts.note: Dot is the usual short form of the name Dorothy
to get on in years is to grow old, to age

explanation.surface: Dorothy carries on gamely though her mind is starting to fail with old age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'despite suffering from' is padding that links the pieces to the definition at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Dotage is the feeble-minded state of extreme old age, a synonym for senility.

clue.text: One who takes great interest in his work

definitions.text: One who takes great interest in his work

parts.words: One who takes great interest in his work
parts.note: read as a keen enthusiast, but 'interest' is money charged on a loan, taken in great amounts

explanation.surface: A dedicated employee who is fascinated by their job.
explanation.definitionFit: A moneylender charging exorbitant rates literally takes great interest as his trade.

clue.text: Frank, outspoken rating describing what a brain cell is

explanation.surface: A description of a neuron offered as a blunt telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving someone this means a frank scolding (a 'rating'); literally a brain cell is one small part of the thinking organ.

clue.text: Unpleasant like Leo perhaps

explanation.surface: Someone born under Leo is called nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Beastly means nasty; literally it means animal-like, as Leo the lion is a beast.

clue.text: It is something a credit customer cannot get

definitions.text: It is something a credit customer cannot get

parts.words: It is something a credit customer cannot get
parts.note: someone buying on credit does not pay at once, so misses the price reduction offered for immediate payment

explanation.surface: A remark about what shoppers who buy on account miss out on.
explanation.definitionFit: A reduction in price granted only to buyers who pay straight away in money rather than on account.

clue.text: Transporter?

parts.note: looks like a vehicle or carrier, but to transport also means to enrapture, to carry away with delight

explanation.surface: A one-word question suggesting a lorry or a removals van.
explanation.definitionFit: To ravish is to fill with delight, the same as to transport emotionally, so one who does so fits.

clue.text: Nora initially was odly restive about having to buy shares again

indicators.note: oddly says the letters that follow are arranged in a strange new order
initially picks out only the opening letter of the name Nora

explanation.surface: Nora, uncharacteristically fidgety, is about to put money back into the stock market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' rearranges N (Nora's first letter, from 'initially') plus RESTIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To put money back into stocks after taking a return is to invest a second time.

clue.text: Miserable existence experienced by Rover?

explanation.surface: A pet called Rover is having a wretched time.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a wretched, harassed life; literally it is the life a pet hound such as Rover leads.

clue.text: The girl is a beldame to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A remark that the young woman is, in some measure, an old hag.
explanation.walkthrough: A beldame is an old woman, which makes the surface a playful insult.
explanation.definitionFit: Isabel is a female first name, so it can stand for a girl.

clue.text: Beastly fool

parts.note: a fool who is also literally a beast: the donkey, whose name is slang for an idiot

explanation.surface: A rude name for a horrible idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: The donkey is an animal whose name is also used for a stupid person.

clue.text: Expresses disapproval at the service accommodation

explanation.surface: A soldier jeers at the quarters the army provides.
explanation.definitionFit: To jeer at a performer is to barrack them; military housing for troops is barracks.

clue.text: Customer has legal right in court

indicators.note: in places the legal right inside the abbreviation for court

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A shopper is entitled to some legal claim when the matter goes before judges.
explanation.definitionFit: A client is someone who buys services from a professional or business, a customer.

clue.text: Funny cries

parts.note: cries read as weeping rather than shouts, and funny as caused by amusement

explanation.surface: Odd shouts or amusing calls.
explanation.definitionFit: Weeping brought on by hilarity is crying that comes from something comic.

clue.text: Girl lost son to another little girl

indicators.note: lost tells us that a part is dropped from the girl's name

parts.note: Alison is a girl's name
taken as written, the word son itself

explanation.surface: A girl gave up her boy to a different young girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Ali is a short girl's name, so it can stand for a little girl.

clue.text: Is cross, troubled by cut

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters of the two words are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed and upset by a reduction.
explanation.definitionFit: To scissor something is to cut it with shears.

clue.text: Cornet substituted in company's musical composition

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company

indicators.note: substituted suggests the letters are swapped around into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A brass instrument is replaced in a firm's piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'substituted' signals the anagram of 'Cornet'; the surface reads it as one brass instrument swapped for another, and 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A concerto is a piece for solo instrument and orchestra, a kind of musical work.

clue.text: Looking villainous in having a relative around

indicators.note: around says the relative wraps itself about the short word

parts.note: a sister is a family relative
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone appears wicked when a family member is close by.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister describes a menacing, evil-seeming appearance.

clue.text: Repeat treat that is riotous

indicators.note: riotous means wild and unruly, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: An instruction to do again a treat that is wild and boisterous.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to say or do something again.

clue.text: A couple of pounds, that's the lot

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound sterling, so two of them make LL

explanation.surface: Two quid is everything I have.
explanation.definitionFit: All means everything, the whole lot.

clue.text: Leading actor perhaps is an astrologer

explanation.surface: A principal performer who also reads horoscopes.
explanation.definitionFit: A star man is a lead performer; a starman, a reader of the heavens, is an astrologer.

clue.text: One French friend accepts design accidentally

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so the design goes within the other pieces

parts.note: un is French for one
an ally is a friend
a design is an aim or purpose, an intention

explanation.surface: A French companion takes on a plan by chance.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something without meaning to is doing it by accident.

clue.text: Beginning to appear but not starting the shelter

indicators.note: not starting tells us the first letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: dawning means beginning to appear, as day or an idea does

explanation.surface: Something emerges, though not the canopy at first.
explanation.definitionFit: An awning is a canvas canopy giving cover from sun or rain.

clue.text: Three learners went round the ring while Edward lounged about

indicators.note: went round says the learners surround the ring

parts.note: L is a learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car
O is ring-shaped
Ed is the short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Three pupils circled a boxing ring as Edward idled.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a learner driver displays an L-plate, so L means learner.
explanation.definitionFit: To loll is to lounge lazily.

clue.text: Streams before morning washed up on shore

indicators.note: before places the streams ahead of the morning in the answer

parts.note: jets are streams of liquid or gas

explanation.surface: Currents ahead of daybreak have brought debris onto the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Jetsam is goods thrown overboard that drift to the beach.

clue.text: Not much money in trust not long ago

indicators.note: in puts the small coin inside the word for trust

parts.note: to rely is to trust
a cent is a small coin, not much money

explanation.surface: Only a little cash has been placed in a fund lately.
explanation.definitionFit: Recently means lately, a short time back.

clue.text: Theory held by a numismatist

indicators.note: held by says the answer is contained within the following word

explanation.surface: A coin collector's pet idea.
explanation.definitionFit: An ism is a doctrine or system of belief.

clue.text: Right amongst various newts that were scattered about

indicators.note: amongst puts the letter for right among the jumbled letters
various suggests the letters of the amphibians are mixed into different order

explanation.surface: Correct among assorted amphibians that had been spread around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' rearranges NEWTS into STEWN, and 'amongst' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Strewn means spread untidily over an area, scattered.

clue.text: He is unable to make his presence felt

definitions.text: He is unable to make his presence felt

parts.words: He is unable to make his presence felt
parts.note: sounds like someone lacking influence, but literally he is not present at all

explanation.surface: A man who has no impact on those around him.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone missing from work or school cannot be felt as present because they are not there.
